Roasted Chestnuts

Served at: Martinstag Lantern Evening

Serves 4Prep 10 minCook 25 min

Roasted chestnuts are a warm, fragrant treat traditionally enjoyed during Martinstag Lantern Evening in Germany. This simple yet festive snack is perfect for sharing while walking with lanterns, embodying the cozy spirit of the holiday.

Ingredients

  • 1 lb (450 g) fresh chestnuts
  • 1 tsp salt
  • Water for soaking

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
  2. Using a sharp knife, carefully cut a small 'X' on the flat side of each chestnut to allow steam to escape during roasting.
  3. Place the chestnuts in a bowl and cover with water; soak for 30 minutes to help soften the shells.
  4. Drain the chestnuts and pat them dry with a towel.
  5. Arrange the chestnuts on a baking sheet in a single layer, cut side up.
  6. Sprinkle with salt evenly over the chestnuts.
  7. Roast in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until the shells curl back and the nuts are tender when pierced with a fork.
  8. Remove from the oven and cover with a clean kitchen towel for 5 minutes to allow them to steam slightly, making peeling easier.
  9. Peel the chestnuts while still warm and serve immediately.

Tips

  • Make sure to cut the 'X' deep enough to pierce the shell but not the nut inside to prevent bursting.
  • If chestnuts are difficult to peel, reheat them slightly or soak in warm water for a few minutes.
  • For added flavor, sprinkle with a little cinnamon or drizzle with honey after roasting.
